profile.reading: AiNET's Beltsville, Maryland facility, identified by the short code WDC-1 on a dedicated Baxtel industry listing, sits at 11700 Montgomery Road, Beltsville, Maryland 20705, and serves as the company's home base. Founded in 1993 as a dial up internet service provider in Maryland, AiNET has grown into a regional data center, colocation, and fiber network operator serving the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor. The Baxtel listing describes this Beltsville building as a fully operational, single floor facility owned outright by AiNET, certified to SAS 70 Type II and TIA-942 standards, though the listing does not publicly disclose square footage or a specific power capacity figure for this building, restricting that detail behind a paid dataset request rather than publishing it openly. AiNET's own site describes the company's broader footprint as spanning the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor, including its larger CyberNAP facility in Glen Burnie, Maryland, a converted 300,000 square foot former department store roughly 10 miles north of Fort Meade, already on file elsewhere in this registry. No square footage or MW figure could be confirmed for this specific Beltsville building this session despite a fresh attempt, an honest gap rather than a fabricated estimate.

reading.body:
AiNET's Beltsville facility, located at 11700 Montgomery Road in Prince George's County, Maryland, is a single-floor, operator-owned data center certified to SAS 70 Type II and TIA-942 standards. The operator publishes no power capacity or square footage for this building, restricting those figures behind a paid dataset request rather than disclosing them on its own site or through industry listings. This gap prevents any estimate of rack density or accelerator capacity at the site.

The facility serves as AiNET's corporate base, built on the operator's 30-year history as a regional colocation and fiber network provider in the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor. AiNET's published footprint includes its larger CyberNAP facility in Glen Burnie, Maryland, a converted 300,000 square-foot former department store roughly 10 miles north of Fort Meade. Without disclosed power or area figures for Beltsville, the relative scale and role of this location within the operator's portfolio cannot be determined from public sources.

Maryland has published power capacity at only 3 of its 11 mapped data center facilities, totaling 9.3 MW across the state. This Beltsville campus ranks fourth by published megawattage among Maryland facilities, though that ranking reflects only the three sites that disclose figures at all. The absence of a published power specification for this building leaves its actual contribution to state capacity and its relevance to grid-constrained AI scaling unknown.
